pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered from 00:30:00 and correctly aimed at the plateau and at supporting rather than replacing his running. He agreed without questions and confirmed globally at 00:36:35: 'I don't, yeah, I don't have any, I don't have any objections anywhere.' Scored accepted rather than enthusiastic because the enthusiasm came before the pitch, not during it — he had already surfaced kettlebells himself at 00:23:42: 'I've never done kettlebells and stuff like that, and I've always been interested in things like that, for strength training... I'm seeing now that that's something that maybe could be more beneficial.' The one correction he made was factual, not a pushback: the rep said '1,500 miles per week' and he replied 'Well, right now, it's 30 miles per week, but you were talking about the whole year.'

Delivered at 00:32:00 as what you eat, when you eat, how much you eat, with the rep opening by validating what he already does ('you already said that you're basically eating clean. That's good'). He agreed — 'That makes sense. Yeah.' — and asked nothing. The rep also pre-empted the obvious objection by protecting his Friday burger night with his kids as sustainable, which the prospect took well. No enthusiasm and no resistance; nutrition was never a live issue on this call.

Delivered at 00:34:00 and explicitly positioned as 'the most important part in your case', which was accurate — the prospect had already named the absence of feedback as his missing piece twenty minutes earlier. Confirmed understanding without a single question: 'Any questions on that? Nope.' Notable that a man who has never worked with any coach and said 'I feel like just somebody that knows and does the same thing... that can recognize ways I can kind of get to where I'm trying to go' had nothing to ask about how the accountability actually works. Understood and agreed, but not probed.

anchors.raw: that's the kind of stuff I'd have to talk to my wife with to keep her involved in everything. Because, you know, money's tight, man. You know, it's everything.
anchors.note: The number in his head when he hears $6,000 is a three-child household budget, not a competing product. He confirmed he does not have the full amount and would proceed immediately if he did, which makes this a pure liquidity anchor rather than a value objection. It is the same shape as the Marian Samson and Fletcher Koder calls: the blocker is the lump sum, not the price.

anchors.raw: I never have, no. I've never done that. It's always just been me, just trying to get, you know, in the best shape as I can
anchors.note: An absence functioning as an anchor. He has never paid for coaching of any kind, so he has no frame for what one-on-one coaching costs and nothing to compare $6,000 against except household spending. He said so explicitly when the price landed: 'I didn't know how much it was going to be.' This is the opposite of the Sasa Svalina call, where a history of paid personal training made the price feel normal.

anchors.raw: the Peloton, I was doing that, you I had the Peloton bike. I would incorporate that, and I'd try to do, like, some yoga stuff, too, stretching, the stretching routines... other than that, it's just been like my Garmin watch
anchors.note: His entire history of paid fitness spend is subscription hardware in the tens of dollars per month. The rep did use this correctly — reframing it as 'scattered' rather than as competition — but it is still the cost frame the prospect is arriving with, and nothing on the call bridged the gap between a Peloton subscription and $6,000.

unmet_demand.want: Marathon-specific coaching capable of taking a 3:51 predictor to a sub-3:10 Boston qualifier in about six months
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This is his headline goal and the rep endorsed the timeline — 'so actually we have six months to work on that, so you can actually go for the qualifier' — without ever establishing that Trevor coaches distance running. What was promised is adaptation around running, not coaching of it: 'Trevor will adapt that program to your running schedule, because that also needs to be adjusted.' The rep's own credential offered on the topic was a personal anecdote about mountain hiking. Whether the programme can deliver a 41-minute marathon improvement is genuinely unknown from this transcript, and a principal should establish it before the Tuesday call.

unmet_demand.want: Technique feedback on his running form, not just on kettlebell movements
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked for feedback in general terms — 'maybe just some feedback, you know... when I do something, not just having my own feedback, and then maybe tips for when I do that.' What was described in return is video review of kettlebell movements specifically: 'when you're going to be learning kettlebells in your first month, like every single movement, you're just going to record yourself, you send it to Trevor.' Running gait was never mentioned. The programme may well cover it; nobody said so.

unmet_demand.want: A way to pay $6,000 that does not require the full amount up front
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep offered the possibility — 'for some clients, we can break it up. Like, don't have anything set in stone, like set payment plans' — and then never proposed any terms, even after the prospect did the arithmetic himself at $1,000 a month. Whether an instalment plan actually exists is unresolved across this batch: the same rep told a different prospect the same week that six instalments were definitively impossible and carried a $1,200 premium.
